lead: Travellers committed to preserving natural and cultural resources will find in Valencia a green city with unique ecosystems and ways of discovering it without generating emissions.

Valencia was named European Green Capital 2024, in recognition of its commitment to urban sustainability, green mobility and the conservation of its natural ecosystems. The Albufera Natural Park, the largest wetland in Spain, is just ten kilometres from the centre and is home to more than 300 species of birds. The Valencian Huerta, protected by the City Council since 2018, is one of the richest peri-urban agricultural landscapes in Europe.

The activities you will find here are organised by responsible ecotourism companies, many run by natives of the natural areas themselves, who combine the travel experience with conservation of the environment and support for local communities.

items.title: Zero emissions
items.body: Prioritise getting around on foot, by bike, by public transport or in rowing and sailing boats.

items.title: Local economy
items.body: Hire local companies, eat in restaurants with local produce and shop in local businesses.

items.title: Leave no trace
items.body: Do not leave waste in natural areas, stay on marked paths and respect wildlife.

items.title: Low capacity
items.body: Choose small groups, visit in low season and avoid natural areas at peak summer hours.

items.title: Boat trip on the Albufera
items.body: The most authentic ecotourism experience in Valencia: travelling the Albufera lake in a traditional albuferenca boat accompanied by native guides of the park. The Albufera Natural Park is the largest wetland in Spain, with more than 21,000 hectares of rice fields, dunes, pine forests and the largest freshwater lake on the Peninsula. The companies Albufera Nature and Albufera Parc offer responsible ecotourism experiences run by people native to the park.

items.title: Birdwatching at the Racó de l’Olla
items.body: The Racó de l’Olla is the most important nature reserve in the Albufera Natural Park: 50 hectares of inland lagoon and marsh vegetation where the largest populations of waterfowl are concentrated. Flamingos, grey herons, red-crested pochards, cormorants and up to 300 different species live in or pass through this area throughout the year. The interpretation centre, the observatory and the lookout tower allow you to watch the birds without disturbing them.

items.title: Bike routes through the Valencian Huerta
items.body: The Valencian Huerta is the oldest and most authentic landscape in Valencia: orange groves, vegetable gardens, traditional barracas and Moorish irrigation channels that have surrounded the city for more than a thousand years. The Metropolitan Green Ring has more than 100 km of signposted cycling and walking routes that let you discover this territory with zero emissions. The Huerta Norte route leads through farmland, barracas and historic farmhouses. The Huerta Sur route shows the contrast between the countryside and the Albufera Natural Park.

items.title: Walking tours of the historic centre
items.body: Valencia is perfect for zero-emission tourism: its historic centre is compact, accessible and full of heritage within walking distance. Walking tours cover unique routes such as the legacy of Silk (declared Intangible Cultural Heritage by UNESCO), the mysteries of the Holy Chalice, the street art of El Carmen, the Serranos and Quart Towers and the World Heritage Sites. Companies of certified local guides offer small-group tours with a historical and cultural focus.

items.title: Sea crossing on a schooner · Cervantes Saavedra
items.body: The training ship Cervantes Saavedra, in collaboration with the Oceanogràfic de Valencia, organises sea crossings with educational and environmental awareness content. The Blue Planet Crossing takes participants through the Mediterranean to Formentera and Cabrera, learning about marine biology, history and ocean conservation. The “Albufera and Oceanogràfic” weekends combine a visit to the wetland with the experience of sailing.

items.title: Monumental Trees Route
items.body: Valencia has more than 500 catalogued monumental trees. Five official routes let you get to know the most singular specimens: trees 400 years old, centuries-old holm oaks, giant eucalyptuses, palms, mulberries, fig trees and exotic species such as the Indian laurel, the ginkgo or the living fossil from China. The routes are self-guided, free and combine natural heritage with the city’s historical heritage.

items.title: Hiking in nearby natural parks
items.body: The province of Valencia has four natural parks less than an hour from the centre, all accessible by public transport or by car. The Turia Natural Park (5,000 hectares of Mediterranean woodland and river) has hiking trails beside the river bed with crystal-clear pools. The Sierra Calderona offers routes with views of the Mediterranean. The Hoces del Cabriel, with the cleanest river in Spain, are the best-kept secret of the province.

items.title: Natural beaches of the Albufera Park
items.body: South of the city of Valencia, the Albufera Natural Park protects kilometres of unspoilt dune beach with free access. El Saler beach, 10 km from the centre, maintains the original dune system with native Mediterranean vegetation. La Devesa beach, within the park, is one of the longest and most natural beaches on the Mediterranean coast. Unlike urban beaches, these protected beaches have no permanent services, in order to preserve the ecosystem.

blocks.title: Responsible traveller’s code in Valencia
items: Use public transport or a bike to reach natural areas: cars at El Saler and the Albufera cause congestion
On the Albufera, hire companies with native guides: part of their income goes to conserving the park
Do not leave waste on natural beaches or dunes: the dune ecosystem is very fragile and hard to recover
Respect the marked paths and the bird observatories: getting too close scares the species away
Choose restaurants with kilometre 0 produce: the paella in El Palmar uses rice from the park itself
The Racó de l’Olla has restricted access at certain times: check the opening hours before you go
